requirements.title: The /graph page shall display a hero row above the board stating the page's identity and a one-line promise inviting interaction

vision.paraphrase: The hero row provides cold-visitor onboarding, stating the page's identity and inviting interaction in one glance.
The hero row is bold page identity plus one-line promise inviting interaction, addressing the finding that the page opened straight into the canvas with no framing (B1).

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor lands on /graph, a hero row is visible above the board, stating the page's identity and what the map contains.

requirements.title: The side panel shall display a "Start anywhere" onboarding card, naming what the map is built from, whenever no node is selected

vision.paraphrase: The start-anywhere card transforms the panel's empty state from wasted onboarding real estate into a guided entry point for cold visitors.
The onboarding panel includes what the map is built from, a color-coded folder legend, and pointers on where to begin.

conops.paraphrase: The side panel's empty state displays a start-anywhere card describing what the map is built from, reducing onboarding friction for first-time visitors.

requirements.title: The start-anywhere card shall display a folder legend mapping each folder/taxonomy color rendered in the graph to that folder's name

vision.paraphrase: The folder legend makes node color-coding meaningful to any visitor, providing the missing key that issue #4 finding B3 surfaced.
The legend shows color-coded key mapping folder colors to their meanings in the start-anywhere panel.

conops.paraphrase: The start-anywhere card displays a legend entry for each folder/taxonomy value, mapping its color to its name.

requirements.title: The start-anywhere card shall display a status legend mapping each status dot style to its meaning for the values active, revisiting, and dormant

vision.paraphrase: The status legend explains the status-dot encoding to visitors, fixing the omission surfaced in issue #4 finding B3 where no legend existed.

conops.paraphrase: The start-anywhere card displays a status legend showing what each status-dot style (active, revisiting, dormant) represents.

requirements.title: The start-anywhere card shall suggest at least one concrete starting point for a visitor who does not know where to begin

vision.paraphrase: Concrete starting-point suggestions reduce decision paralysis for cold visitors, helping them begin exploring within seconds.

conops.paraphrase: The start-anywhere card suggests a concrete first action, such as clicking a hub node or searching for a topic, guiding the visitor's first interaction.

requirements.title: The side panel shall replace the start-anywhere card with the selected node's detail when a visitor selects a node

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor clicks a suggested node, the start-anywhere card is replaced by that node's detail.

requirements.title: The side panel shall restore the start-anywhere card when the visitor clears the current node selection

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor clears the node selection, the side panel returns to the start-anywhere card, ready to guide the next exploration.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall display a stats footer presenting the vault's ingested source count, wiki page count, and connection count as a single derivation reading "Built from K raw sources → Y wiki pages and Z connections"

vision.section: §6 — MVP Scope Summary (Demo-Quality Upgrade: Stats footer)
vision.paraphrase: Presents the three figures as one raw→wiki derivation rather than three loose counts, because that derivation is the knowledge-work technique the whole artifact exists to evidence. '40 sources became 142 interlinked pages' is a claim a visitor can check; a bare node count is trivia.

conops.paraphrase: A cold visitor reads the footer to judge whether the vault is real. The provenance sentence answers that in one glance and stays spot-checkable against the source links themselves.

amended.reason: Reworded from three independent counts ('N nodes · M connections · built from K sources') to a single provenance sentence ('Built from K raw sources → Y wiki pages and Z connections') at the author's direction, making the raw→wiki pipeline legible. Plain wording chosen over the project's internal 'ingest'/'raw source file' vocabulary, since the footer serves cold-visitor onboarding. Not a change-control event — authored this cycle, unmerged.

requirements.title: The stats footer shall display an "Esc to reset" hint describing the Esc key's behavior on the page

vision.paraphrase: The Esc hint advertises the keyboard de-escalation feature, enabling keyboard-driven visitors to manage page state.

conops.paraphrase: The stats footer displays a hint indicating that Esc resets the current view state, matching the de-escalation chain behavior.
The Esc hint advertises the keyboard de-escalation chain so keyboard-driven visitors know the affordance exists.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall display a persistent "Take a tour" control that starts the guided tour when activated

vision.paraphrase: A single Take a tour control steps through 4–5 curated linked nodes with captions, providing guided entry for visitors unsure where to start.
The guided tour is a persistent control that steps the visitor through a hand-curated walk.

conops.paraphrase: A visible Take a tour control is present on the page, allowing a visitor to initiate the guided tour at any time.

requirements.title: The guided tour shall be driven by a static hand-curated tour definition of between 4 and 5 node ids with a caption for each step

vision.paraphrase: The tour path and captions are hand-curated against the demo vault and shipped as a static asset, not auto-generated.

conops.paraphrase: The static tour-definition asset shipped with the application defines an ordered list of 4–5 curated node ids with captions per step.

requirements.title: The guided tour shall focus each step's node in the active layout mode and display that node's detail alongside the step's tour caption

vision.paraphrase: The tour rides the existing per-mode selection behavior (force-directed center/zoom or swim-lane connector animation) rather than defining a third one.

conops.paraphrase: When the tour advances to a step, the graph focuses that node using the active layout mode's selection behavior, and the side panel displays the node's detail plus the tour caption.

requirements.title: The guided tour shall advance to the next node in the curated path when the visitor activates the "Next" control, with each consecutive pair of steps connected by a real edge in the graph

vision.paraphrase: Tour steps connected by real edges demonstrate the graph's navigation rather than merely slideshowing through nodes.

conops.paraphrase: When the visitor activates Next, the tour advances to the next curated node, with each step following a real edge in the graph.

requirements.title: The guided tour shall display a step indicator reporting the current step number and the total number of steps

conops.paraphrase: The tour displays a step indicator showing the current step number and total steps, orienting the visitor through the curated path.

requirements.title: The guided tour shall offer an "Explore on your own" control at its final step that exits the tour when activated

conops.paraphrase: At the tour's final step, a control invites the visitor to explore on their own, cleanly exiting the tour.

requirements.title: The guided tour shall leave the current step's node selected in the graph and side panel when the tour is exited

conops.paraphrase: When the tour exits, the step's node remains selected with the side panel still showing its detail, handing the visitor the thread they were holding.

requirements.title: The /graph page's stats footer shall omit the provenance clause entirely, displaying only the page and connection counts, when the vault declares no ingested sources

vision.paraphrase: Protects the generic-tool claim against the new footer wording. A provenance sentence that only reads correctly against this project's own vault layout would quietly make the page vault-specific; omitting the clause keeps any Karpathy-pattern wiki renderable.
Third-party vaults are an anticipated future use, and those will generally have no raw/ sibling, so the footer must already degrade truthfully rather than print 'Built from 0 raw sources'.

conops.paraphrase: The footer's purpose is establishing credibility in the first seconds; rendering a zero-source provenance claim would destroy exactly the trust it exists to build. Saying nothing is the truthful rendering when a vault has no provenance to declare.
